subject: general
question: Who developed the concept of 'human development'?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Mahbub-ul-Haq**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• 
 
**Dr. Mahbub-ul-Haq **was the **one who first presented **the **idea of human development**.

 
 
• 
 
**According to Dr. Haq**, human **growth expands **people's options and **enhances their quality of life**.

 
 
• 
 
**According to this **theory, people are at **the center of all progress**.

 
 
• 
 
The **inaugural Human Development Report **unveiled a **novel strategy **for **enhancing human welfare in 1990**.

 
 
• 
 
The **goal of human development**, or the **human development approach**, is to **increase **the **richness **of human life rather **than only the economy in which people live**.

 
 
• 
 
**Mahbub ul Haq **was a **politician**, **economist**, and **thinker of international development from Pakistan**.

 
 
• 
 
From **10 April 1985 to 28 **January **1986 **and again as a caretaker from **June to December 1988**, he was **Pakistan's minister of finance**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Amartya Kumar Sen **is an **Indian economist **and **philosopher**, who **since 1972 **has taught and **worked **in the **United Kingdom **and the **United States**. He **gets awarded **the **1998 Nobel Prize **in **Economic Sciences **for his contributions to **welfare economics **and **social choice theory **and for his **interest **in the **problems **of **society's poorest members**.
 
• The **Dalai Lama **was **forced **to **flee **his **home of Tibet **in **1959 **after China sent troops into the region. He sought **refuge in India and for six decades **has been living in exile in Dharamsala along with some 10,000 Tibetans.
 
• **Charles Robert Darwin **was an **English naturalist**, **geologist **and **biologist**, best known for **his contributions to evolutionary biology**.
